questions.question: Which HTTP method appends form data directly into the browser URL query string?
options: POST
GET
PUT
PATCH
questions.hint: Used for searches and bookmarked pages.
questions.explanation: The GET method encodes form data into URL query parameters (?key=value).

questions.question: Why must sensitive credentials like passwords never be sent via method="GET"?
options: GET requests encrypt passwords twice, causing decryption failures
The passwords will be exposed in plain text in browser history and server logs
GET requests are blocked on mobile networks
The browser refuses to submit fields containing numbers
questions.hint: Look at where GET places its data.
questions.explanation: GET puts parameter values directly in the URL, exposing passwords in browser history, bookmarks, and server log files.

questions.question: What happens if an <input> element does not have a name attribute when the form is submitted?
options: The form errors out with a JavaScript runtime error
The input value is omitted from the submission payload entirely
The browser generates a random hexadecimal name
The input is converted to read-only
questions.hint: The name attribute forms the key in the key-value pair.
questions.explanation: Only form controls with a valid 'name' attribute have their values transmitted upon submission.

questions.question: Which enctype attribute value is mandatory when submitting file attachments via a form?
options: multipart/form-data
application/x-www-form-urlencoded
text/plain
binary/octets
questions.explanation: enctype="multipart/form-data" instructs the browser to stream binary file data across multiple body parts.

questions.question: What does the action attribute on a <form> element specify?
options: The CSS transition animation to run upon clicking submit
The server endpoint URL where form data should be sent
The validation regex applied to input fields
The user permission level required to edit the form
questions.explanation: The action attribute points to the URL that will process the submitted form data.
